M1 Cross-Validation Notes — Python client vs C++ client
=========================================================

Status: Deferred (C++ client binary not available in dev environment).

The M1 acceptance criteria require running the C++ client on the same YAML+sizes
and comparing GFLOPs and tensor values.  This step was not completed during the
initial implementation because the C++ client binary (hipblaslt-bench or the
Tensile benchmark runner) was not built and installed in the development
environment used to write and commit this milestone.

Blocker resolution:
  The C++ client cross-validation must be performed by the reviewer (or a CI job)
  before M2 may begin.  Any GFLOPS divergence greater than ±5%, or any tensor-value
  mismatch, is a blocker per the acceptance criteria.

How to re-run the validation:
  1. Build the C++ client:
       invoke build -ca gfx950 -c --clean
  2. Run hipblaslt-bench (or the Tensile benchmark runner) against the same
     problem sizes in gemm_standard.yaml:
       hipblaslt-bench --function gemm --datatype f32_r \
         --transposeA N --transposeB T \
         --batch 4 --m 256 --n 256 --k 256 \
         ...
  3. Run the Python client on the same sizes via test_gemm_standard.py
     (printing GFLOPs from BenchmarkResult.gflops()).
  4. Compare GFLOPS per problem; record results in this file in the format:
       PROBLEM         PY_GFLOPS   CPP_GFLOPS   DELTA%
       256x256x4x256   <value>     <value>      <±%>
       ...
  5. If any delta > 5%, root-cause (thermal noise, mismatched configuration,
     argument-construction bug) and document here before marking M1 complete.

Tensor-value comparison:
  Use `assertClose` from Tensile/client/reference.py with RTOL/ATOL constants
  from that module.  Any mismatch at the validated tolerance is a blocker.

Note:
  The poison-input test in test_gemm_standard.py (test_buildKernelArgs_poison)
  verifies that the argument buffer actually drives the computation by corrupting
  strideA[1] and confirming that more than 50% of output elements are wrong.
  This test must pass before any correctness claim is valid.
